title: Is it Too Late to Buy UnitedHealth Stock? | UNH Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garble the DCF fair value and current price figures, so they are not stated here
summary: Parkevtate revisits UnitedHealth after its 2026 recovery from the 2025 crisis, when the company underestimated the cost of serving customers, mispriced policies and saw profitability and free cash flow collapse. Management promised improvements from 2026 and has delivered slightly better than forecast, with the shares up almost 20% year to date, so he asks whether it is still a buy. The key evidence is Wall Street's change of mind: analysts who had cut EPS growth estimates to flat or negative have now revised them back above 14.2%, near the midpoint of management's 13-16% long-term guide. The balance sheet has also strengthened: long-term debt has been cut by about $9 billion in 2026, from roughly $80 billion to just over $71.4 billion, which should reduce interest expense and free cash for further debt paydown or the aggressive buybacks of the last 12-18 months. Valuation has improved but not dramatically: the forward P/E is 17, still below pre-2025 levels, which he calls attractive against 13-16% expected EPS growth. The caveat is that costs did not fall, they were merely estimated correctly this time, so structurally higher costs persist, and the company has exited some markets and raised prices, serving fewer customers. His updated DCF also shows the stock undervalued, though the exact fair value and current price figures are garbled in the captions. He concludes UnitedHealth remains a buying opportunity, a first tracked BUY for him, with a worthwhile risk-reward.
